chunks: "Doping improves silicon in a few separate ways. The first and most obvious is conductivity.

Pure silicon has about 10 to the 10 carriers per cm³, and doping with 10 to the 16 per cm³ boosts that by a factor of a million, so resistivity drops from hundreds of kilohm-centimetres to around half an ohm-centimetre.
The second is control. Intrinsic carrier density doubles about every 10 degrees, so undoped silicon would drift wildly with temperature.
With doping, the carrier density is fixed by the dopant count, and it stays put from below room temperature to a few hundred degrees C.
The third is that I get to choose the carrier type. Without N and P regions I can't make a junction, so no diode, no BJT, no MOSFET. And fourth, I can tune a device.
Light doping in a drift region gives high breakdown voltage; heavy doping in the source, drain, emitter and contact regions gives low resistance; channel doping sets the MOSFET threshold.
The caveat is that more isn't always better.
Heavy doping lowers mobility, narrows the depletion region so breakdown voltage and leakage get worse, and past solid solubility extra dopant doesn't even add carriers."
